sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 601.7 ± 91.6 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by M1 anti-FLAG labeling of non-permeabilized HEK293T cells (L2/L4); BRET/NanoBiT assay demonstrates the receptor is functional at the cell surface (L1); TANGO assay (a GPCR activation reporter) confirms surface expression and receptor activation competence (L5/L6).
sites.rationale: DRD4 has no endogenous signal peptide; its N-terminus (residues 1–33) is extracellular per the topology landmarks. All six N-terminal tag clips add an exogenous cleavable signal peptide upstream of a FLAG or HA tag; after SP cleavage the tag is displayed at the extracellular face immediately before residue M1, making insert_after_residue=0 the only possible junction. Python confirmed residue 1 is M and TM1 begins at residue 34, placing the tag 33 residues from the nearest TM boundary. No specific residue number is cited in any clip, but for a GPCR the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus, so the position is topology-derived rather than inferred. Full-length D4R (D4.4R) expressed in HEK293 cells with an exogenous cleavable HA signal peptide followed by a FLAG tag prepended to the receptor N-terminus; the construct also carries a C-terminal NanoBiT NP tag and is used in surface-expression-based BRET/NanoBiT assays. Multiple independent groups (PMC9911804, PMC9112046, PMC4424118) report the same N-terminal FLAG or HA architecture on full-length membrane-anchored DRD4.

sources.claim: Thus, in addition to the C-terminal linker (GNSGSSGGGGSGGGGSSG) and NP tag (GVTGWRLCERILA), D 4 R-NP contained an N-terminal cleavable influenza hemagglutinin signal peptide (KTIIALSYIFCLVFA) to promote surface expression, followed by a FLAG tag (DYKDDDDK).

literature_notes: Six ledger lines (L1–L6) all support the same N-terminal extracellular tag site on full-length membrane-anchored DRD4; they differ only in tag type (FLAG vs HA) and assay context (BRET, TANGO, immunofluorescence) but all converge on insert_after_residue=0. L7 and L8 describe a cpGFP insertion replacing residues R217–W306, which Python confirmed lies entirely within the large intracellular loop ICL3 (topology span 215–346); this is a tolerated intracellular insertion and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports a tag in ECL1 (94–108), ECL2 (172–191), or ECL3 (368–382), so no internal extracellular loop sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: cpGFP module inserted replacing segment R217(5.67)–W306(6.28) in the large ICL3 (intracellular span 215–346); receptor retains significant agonist and antagonist response (L8), but the site is cytoplasmic and not accessible for extracellular surface tagging.
